title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page continues a combinatorial description of a 'carte' (dessin d'enfant), viewed as an oriented triangulated surface of type {0,1,∞}. The flags r ∈ R are the triangles of the barycentric-type triangulation. The involutions σ_k / τ_k (k ∈ {0,1,∞}) exchange r with the adjacent flag across the side opposite the vertex of type k. X is the compact Riemann surface given by the canonical conformal realisation of the map. S is the set of all vertices R_φ (types 0, 1, ∞).

The blown-up surface. Grothendieck forms X̃^{***}: X with the points of type 0, 1, ∞ removed in the sense of a surface with boundary. Each vertex is replaced by a circle of directions, i.e. the real oriented blow-up. The three stars are arranged in the superscript like the triangle: ∞ at the top, 0 at bottom left, 1 at bottom right. Replacing a star by a dot means that type of vertex is not blown up, giving variants such as X̃^{*·*}. The interior of X̃ is X∖S = X^{**}.

Why the blow-up. The points R_r^{ij} and the arcs of the previous page are now honest points and paths in X̃, canonical and not merely defined up to homotopy. R_r^{ij} is the point on the boundary circle over the type-i vertex of r, in the direction of the side towards the type-j vertex. The R_φ themselves make no sense in X̃. They are recovered via the canonical C^∞ (not real-analytic) map (11) X̃ → X, which sends R_r^{ij} to R_r^i = R_φ.

The cell structure.
- λ_r^i are the arcs of the boundary circle around the type-i vertex, one per flag.
- a_r^i are the segments of the side opposite vertex i. They are shared by r and τ_i r, which is relation (10).
- Each flag r gives a truncated triangle (a hexagon) whose boundary alternates a's and λ's. Its contractibility gives relation (12): b_r^∞ b_r^1 b_r^0 = 1, with b = λ^{-1} a, a loop at R_r^{1∞}.

Conclusion. The vertices R_r^{ij} (identified by (7)), the arrows λ, a, and the relations (10), (12) present the fundamental groupoid π_1(X̃, {R_r^{ij}}). By homotopy equivalence this is also the fundamental groupoid of X∖S with these 'tangential' base points. The purpose is a fully combinatorial, symmetric presentation of π_1 of the punctured surface with base points indexed by flags × ordered pairs of types. It serves the study of the Galois action on such groupoids (Teichmüller/dessins programme). The next page specialises to compute rotations around vertices.
errors: As transcribed on the previous page, (9) gives a_r^i : R_r^{i+1,i} → R_r^{i+1,i+2}. Both endpoints would then sit near the same vertex, which is incompatible with (10) and with the composability in (12). Consistency requires a_r^i to run along the side opposite vertex i, between R^{i+1,i+2} and R^{i+2,i+1}. This is either a transcription error or a slip in the manuscript.
Relation (12) is stated 'dans π_1 X^{**}', while the base point lies on the boundary of X̃. This is harmless via the homotopy equivalence X^{**} ⊂ X̃, which Grothendieck himself notes.
The labelling of the b's (which b gets superscript 0, 1, ∞) is not fully legible; the hexagon relation itself is correct.

ideas.what: Replacing punctures by boundary circles (surface with boundary X̃) with a canonical C^∞ but non-analytic map X̃ → X, with notation recording which vertex types are blown up
ideas.modern_name: real oriented blow-up / Kato–Nakayama-type log space
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard topology; in arithmetic contexts A'Campo, Kato–Nakayama (1999)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses fundamental groupoids with well-chosen base points 'at infinity' but not, as far as I know, this explicit construction

ideas.what: Base points on boundary circles, indexed by flag and direction of an edge at a vertex, used as a canonical base-point set for the fundamental groupoid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'); Ihara, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) speaks of groupoids with base-point sets stable under symmetries

ideas.what: Presentation of π_1(X̃, {R_r^{ij}}) by flag-indexed generators λ, a with gluing relations (10) and hexagon relations (12)
ideas.modern_name: CW/van Kampen presentation of the fundamental groupoid of a dessin complement; cartographic group
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Grothendieck, Malgrange, Jones–Singerman for cartographic groups

missed.claim: Grothendieck uses boundary points of the real blow-up at the vertices, in the direction of the edges, as canonical base points for a Galois-oriented study of π_1 of dessin complements. This is essentially tangential base points attached to a dessin, in a manuscript dated from 1978 onward, predating Deligne's 1989 formalisation. The base-point set is the flag-indexed set R × {ordered pairs of types}, combinatorially determined by the map.
missed.quote: Les points R_r^{ij} et les chemins précédents seront regardés, plus commodément, comme points et chemins (parfaitement canoniques ...) dans X̃^{**}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and motivation for tangential base points in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. It also offers a natural Galois-equivariant groupoid attached to any dessin, convenient for computing Galois actions on dessins via groupoid cocycles.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics (blow-up, CW presentation of a fundamental groupoid) is routine. The notable point is the early, explicit use of boundary or tangential base points indexed by flags for Galois purposes, which is consistent with but more concrete than the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: 'des points comme seuls ∞•1' should read 'disposés comme suit' followed by a small diagram (∞ on top, 0 bottom left, 1 bottom right): the stars in X̃^{***} are placed like the triangle's vertices.
The parenthesis likely reads '(parfaitement canoniques, pas seulement des classes d'homotopie !)', not 'perfectionnement canonique près ...'.
The following passage likely reads '(On notera que les R_φ (φ∈S) n'ont pas de sens dans X̃^{**} - mais il y a l'application C^∞ (non analytique réelle) canonique (11) X̃^{**} → X'.
'basé en R_r^{1∞}' after (12) is probably 'lacet en R_r^{1∞}'.
Last line: 'présentation du groupoïde π_1(X̃^{**}, (R_r^{ij}))', with the relations cited being (10) and (12).
